summary.oneLiner: Kalyan Jewellers delivered exceptional Q4FY26 with 66% revenue and 118% PAT growth, driven by robust non-South expansion and a sharp turnaround in Candere profitability. The strategic pivot to a capital-light FOCO model and imminent elimination of non-GML debt in India positions the company for sustained ROCE expansion despite high gold price volatility.

one-line thesis: Kalyan Jewellers delivered exceptional Q4FY26 with 66% revenue and 118% PAT growth, driven by robust non-South expansion and a sharp turnaround in Candere profitability. The strategic pivot to a capital-light FOCO model and imminent elimination of non-GML debt in India positions the company for sustained ROCE expansion despite high gold price volatility.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 10,275 Cr (+66% YoY); EBITDA/PBT: INR 539 Cr (+115% YoY); PAT: INR 410 Cr (+118% YoY); Order Book: N/A (Retail); Net Debt: Non-GML reduced by INR 360 Cr in FY26 to ~INR 300 Cr, targeting zero in FY27. One-offs: Interest cost inflated by ~INR 30 Cr due to advance tax interest and timing of debt repayments in H1.
guidance: Revenue Growth: High teens to 20%+ implied by 150 new stores; Margin: India PBT ~5.5-5.6%, Candere GM mid-30s; Order Inflow: Strong Akshaya Tritiya start; Capex: Minimal for FOCO, focused on inventory for COCO/hybrid.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Retail business model relies on same-store sales growth (SSSG) and new store ramp-ups rather than traditional order books. Current SSSG trends >20% in recent quarters.
segment / subsidiary detail: India: Rev INR 8,990 Cr (+68%), PAT INR 366 Cr (+97%). Middle East: Rev INR 1,074 Cr (+37%), PAT INR 21 Cr. Candere: Rev INR 131 Cr (+368%), turned PAT positive (INR 3 Cr vs loss of INR 12 Cr).
growth verticals / optionality: 150 new stores planned in FY27 (50-55 Candere, rest Kalyan); Potential conversion of Middle East FOCO to franchisee model unlocking ~INR 800-1000 Cr cash flow; New regional brand launch pending political clarity in target state.
margins & cost dynamics: India gross margins pressured by mix (FOCO vs COCO) and seasonality; Candere commands mid-30% GM due to >70% studded mix. FY26 GM benefited from silver/platinum tailwinds (~INR 20 Cr) which are non-recurring. Operating leverage expected to offset commodity mix headwinds.
capex / expansion: Capital light strategy via FOCO (Franchisee Owned, Company Operated). Capex primarily for COCO renovations, hybrid store upgrades, and inventory funding. Free cash flow prioritized for debt reduction and dividends.
capital allocation: 50% of cash flow allocated to dividends (20% payout ratio declared) and debt reduction; 50% reserved for Candere expansion, new regional brand, and inventory buildup. Target: Zero non-GML debt in India by FY27.
risks & watch-items: Gold price volatility suppressing volume growth; Adhik-Maas (leap month) causing Q1 wedding demand shift; Geopolitical tension affecting Middle East operations; Execution risk on new regional brand launch.
management quality / tone: Confident and pragmatic; Emphasizes volume discipline over value growth during high gold price regimes; Cautious on guiding specific SSSG numbers despite strong momentum; Transparent on one-off interest costs.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly guides to conservative 10% SSSG for long-term modeling despite 20-30% recent runs to manage expectations; Volume growth is actively managed by shifting customers to lower karat (18K/14K) and studded jewelry as gold prices rise, preserving revenue despite lower gram sales.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High gold prices typically suppress volume demand for traditional retailers. | Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd | beneficiary | High | Successfully mitigated volume risk by shifting mix to studded jewelry and lower karat options, while FOCO model reduces capital intensity allowing aggressive expansion even in high-rate environments. |
| Rising interest rates and working capital needs pressure margins for debt-heavy peers. | Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd | beneficiary | High | Imminent elimination of non-GML debt in India will remove ~INR 30 Cr annual interest burden, creating a structural margin advantage over competitors still carrying unsecured debt. |
| Digital-first players eroding market share in lightweight segment. | Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Candere sub-brand turned profitable in Q4 with >70% studded mix, proving ability to compete in digital/lightweight space without compromising group margins. |

themes.title: Jewellery & wedding-economy formalization
themes.need: Organized jewellery is gaining share via capital-light FOCO expansion and GST/hallmarking formalization, even amid record gold-price volatility. KALYANKJIL posted Q4 revenue +66% YoY with 150 new FY27 stores and a near-zero non-GML-debt target; SENCO/PNGJL/DPABHUSHAN ride regional formalization; SKYGOLD/RGL/GOLDIAM on B2B and lab-grown export; KALAMANDIR on the wedding-wear economy.
themes.driver: Akshaya Tritiya / wedding-season demand; FOCO store rollout; gold-price stabilization lifting volumes.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Established in 1993 by Mr. T.S. Kalyanaraman on a 100-year-old family legacy that began with a Kerala textile mill in 1908; the deck claims Kalyan is "[a]mongst [f]ew [b]usiness [h]ouses [w]ith [o]ver 100 [y]ears [l]egacy in [c]orporate India".
- Ten "Key Pillars of Strength" are claimed, led by a trusted brand built on transparency (BIS hallmarking before the regulatory mandate, karatmeter purity checks, component-level price tags, transparent gold exchange), pan-India presence, and a hyperlocal strategy.
- Organised jewellery market share stated at ~7% (source: MOFSL), positioned against an industry where the organised share is shown rising from 5% in 2000 to 40% in 2025 (Technopak).
- Hyperlocal model — localised brand campaigns and regional ambassadors, local-language staff, locally tuned product portfolios (e.g. Thane Maharashtrian, Vashi South Indian, Borivali Gujarati & North Indian, Ghatkopar Gujarati) — is claimed to have "created significant barriers to entry".
- Governance framing: Board chaired by an Independent Director (Vinod Rai, former CAG of India); Walker Chandiok & Co LLP took over as statutory auditor from Deloitte with effect from August 2024.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Credit rating] Rating progression shown as A+ (Stable) in FY2023 and FY2024, enhanced to A+ (Positive) in FY2025 and to AA- (Stable) in FY2026, with "[f]urther enhancement expected" in FY2027.
- [Guidance] "Target same stores sales growth of mid to high single digits" is the stated same-store growth ambition.
- [Gold sourcing] Share of recycled gold in India stood at 46% during Q1FY27, versus 30% in Q1FY26 and 31% in Q4FY26; gross margin was said to be impacted by the higher proportion of exchanged gold and promotional offers under the exchange campaign.
- [One-off] "~Rs 41 Cr one-off gain from import duty hike during the quarter" (India), and a Rs 415 Mn exceptional item recognised due to changes in employee benefit provisions arising from the New Labour Codes.
- [Ownership history] Warburg Pincus invested equity in 2014 with an incremental investment in 2017; the company listed on NSE & BSE via IPO in 2021 and a Warburg Pincus MD (Anish Kumar Saraf) sits on the Board as a Non-Executive Director.
